title: The wrong sunrise
setting: A Saturday in autumn, around five in the afternoon. Kenji, Yuki's little brother, gamed through the night and slept all day. He shuffles into the living room, where his mother is, as the low sun shines in through the window.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: ohayou. a, yabai! mou hi ga nobotteru! okureru!
lines.ja: おはよう。あ、やばい！もう日が昇ってる！遅れる！
lines.kana: おはよう。あ、やばい！もうひがのぼってる！おくれる！
lines.english: Morning. Oh no! The sun's already up! I'm going to be late!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: nani itteru no. ima goji da yo. mou sugu hi ga kureru yo.
lines.ja: 何言ってるの。今五時だよ。もうすぐ日が暮れるよ。
lines.kana: なにいってるの。いまごじだよ。もうすぐひがくれるよ。
lines.english: What are you on about? It's five o'clock. It'll be dark soon.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, goji? jaa, hi ga nobotteru n ja nakute, shizundeku tokoro?
lines.ja: え、五時？じゃあ、日が昇ってるんじゃなくて、沈んでくところ？
lines.kana: え、ごじ？じゃあ、ひがのぼってるんじゃなくて、しずんでくところ？
lines.english: Huh, five? So the sun isn't up, it's on its way down?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sou yo. mata asa made geemu shiteta n desho.
lines.ja: そうよ。また朝までゲームしてたんでしょ。
lines.kana: そうよ。またあさまでゲームしてたんでしょ。
lines.english: That's right. You were gaming till morning again, weren't you?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un. chotto dake tte omotta n da kedo, ki ga tsuitara hi ga nobotteta.
lines.ja: うん。ちょっとだけって思ったんだけど、気がついたら日が昇ってた。
lines.kana: うん。ちょっとだけっておもったんだけど、きがついたらひがのぼってた。
lines.english: Yeah. I only meant to play for a bit, but next thing I knew, the sun was up.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: mou. saikin wa hi ga kureru no ga hayai n da kara, sonna ni netetara ichinichi sugu owatchau yo.
lines.ja: もう。最近は日が暮れるのが早いんだから、そんなに寝てたら一日すぐ終わっちゃうよ。
lines.kana: もう。さいきんはひがくれるのがはやいんだから、そんなにねてたらいちにちすぐおわっちゃうよ。
lines.english: Honestly. It gets dark so early these days. Sleep that long and the day's gone in no time.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: ii jan, doyoubi da shi. a, hi ga shizunjatta.
lines.ja: いいじゃん、土曜日だし。あ、日が沈んじゃった。
lines.kana: いいじゃん、どようびだし。あ、ひがしずんじゃった。
lines.english: So what, it's Saturday. Oh, the sun's gone down.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: hora, hi ga kurete kita. denki tsukete.
lines.ja: ほら、日が暮れてきた。電気つけて。
lines.kana: ほら、ひがくれてきた。でんきつけて。
lines.english: See, it's getting dark. Turn the light on.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: hai hai. a, mite. atchi, tsuki ga deteru.
lines.ja: はいはい。あ、見て。あっち、月が出てる。
lines.kana: はいはい。あ、みて。あっち、つきがでてる。
lines.english: Okay, okay. Oh, look. Over there, the moon's out.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: honto da. kirei ne. kyou wa mangetsu da tte.
lines.ja: ほんとだ。きれいね。今日は満月だって。
lines.kana: ほんとだ。きれいね。きょうはまんげつだって。
lines.english: Oh, so it is. Isn't it lovely? Apparently it's a full moon tonight.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: hi ga shizunde, tsuki ga dete. kyou, nani mo shitenai.
lines.ja: 日が沈んで、月が出て。今日、何もしてない。
lines.kana: ひがしずんで、つきがでて。きょう、なにもしてない。
lines.english: The sun's gone down, the moon's come out, and I haven't done a thing today.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: dakara itta desho. konban wa, hi ga noboru made geemu shinaide ne.
lines.ja: だから言ったでしょ。今晩は、日が昇るまでゲームしないでね。
lines.kana: だからいったでしょ。こんばんは、ひがのぼるまでゲームしないでね。
lines.english: See, I told you. Tonight, no gaming till the sun comes up, okay?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: wakatta. jaa, tsuki ga deteru aida dake ni suru.
lines.ja: わかった。じゃあ、月が出てる間だけにする。
lines.kana: わかった。じゃあ、つきがでてるあいだだけにする。
lines.english: Fine. Then I'll only play while the moon's out.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: mangetsu da yo? sore, asa made desho!
lines.ja: 満月だよ？それ、朝まででしょ！
lines.kana: まんげつだよ？それ、あさまででしょ！
lines.english: It's a full moon, remember? That's till morning!

choices.english: Kenji gets up early to watch the sunrise, but he's too late and misses it.
Kenji wakes up at five in the evening after gaming all night, and at first thinks the setting sun is the sunrise.
Kenji oversleeps on a school day, and his mother tells him he'll be late for school.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-3: Kenji wakes up, sees the low sun and says mou hi ga nobotteru! okureru!, thinking it's morning. His mother tells him it's five and mou sugu hi ga kureru (it'll be dark soon), and he realises the sun isn't coming up but going down (shizundeku tokoro). Lines 4-5: he gamed until the sun came up (ki ga tsuitara hi ga nobotteta) and then slept all day. A is wrong: he never meant to watch a sunrise; the 'sunrise' he saw was the sunset. C is wrong: okureru! was only his sleepy panic. It's Saturday (line 7) and five in the afternoon.

questions.english: On an autumn afternoon you run into Satou-san, your elderly neighbour, outside. He says: "It's only five, but it's already like night out here." Agree, and say how early it gets dark these days.
questions.ja: まだ五時なのに、外はもう夜ですね。
questions.kana: まだごじなのに、そとはもうよるですね。
questions.romaji: mada goji na noni, soto wa mou yoru desu ne.
questions.answer: Agree politely (he's your elderly neighbour) and use hi ga kureru: sou desu ne, hi ga kureru no ga hayaku narimashita ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: sou desu ne. hi ga kureru no ga hayaku narimashita ne.
modelAnswers.ja: そうですね。日が暮れるのが早くなりましたね。
modelAnswers.english: It's true. It gets dark so much earlier now, doesn't it?

modelAnswers.romaji: hontou desu ne. saikin wa hi ga kureru no ga hayai desu ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 本当ですね。最近は日が暮れるのが早いですね。
modelAnswers.english: You're right. It gets dark early these days, doesn't it?

questions.explanation: The evenings drawing in is hi ga kureru, the classic autumn remark: Okaasan says saikin wa hi ga kureru no ga hayai (line 6) and mou sugu hi ga kureru yo (line 2). Kureru here is the day closing, not kureru 'give me'. Kuraku naru no ga hayaku narimashita ne (it gets dark earlier) says the same thing, and people also say hi ga ochiru no ga hayai. Hi ga shizumu is the sun itself going down at a given moment (line 7: a, hi ga shizunjatta), not the evening coming on. Use -masu forms with Satou-san.

questions.english: When Kenji first wakes up and sees the sun through the window, what does he say?
questions.ja: ケンジは最初に何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじはさいしょになんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji wa saisho ni nan to iimashita ka?
questions.explanation: Line 1: mou hi ga nobotteru! He says it again in line 5 (ki ga tsuitara hi ga nobotteta), and his mother uses it in line 12 (hi ga noboru made). Nobotteru means the sun is up now, not that it is in the middle of rising. A: agaru is the everyday 'go up' (stairs, prices), and English 'rise' points to it, but it isn't the usual verb for the sun: the sun noboru. B: okiteru is 'up' as in awake. People and pets okiru; the sun doesn't.

questions.english: On a hot summer evening, Kenta asks if you want to head out for your walk now: "Man, it's hot. Shall we go for our walk now?" Suggest waiting until the sun has gone down.
questions.ja: 暑いね。散歩、今から行く？
questions.kana: あついね。さんぽ、いまからいく？
questions.romaji: atsui ne. sanpo, ima kara iku?
questions.answer: Suggest going once the sun is down, with hi ga shizumu in the -tara or -te kara form: hi ga shizundara ikou.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, hi ga shizundara ikou yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、日が沈んだら行こうよ。
modelAnswers.english: Nah, let's go once the sun's down.

modelAnswers.romaji: mada atsui kara, hi ga shizunde kara ni shiyou.
modelAnswers.ja: まだ暑いから、日が沈んでからにしよう。
modelAnswers.english: It's still hot, so let's wait until the sun's gone down.

questions.explanation: The sun going below the horizon is hi ga shizumu, the same verb as a ship sinking: Kenji says a, hi ga shizunjatta (line 7) and hi ga shizunde, tsuki ga dete (line 11). Not hi ga oriru or hi ga sagaru: English 'go down' points there, but the sun sinks. Hi ga ochiru is also natural in chat. Hi ga kuretara ikou would also be fine Japanese, but it means after dark, a little later: in lines 7-8 the sun goes down first (shizunjatta) and only then does it get dark (hi ga kurete kita).

questions.english: At the end, what does Kenji say he'll do tonight?
questions.ja: ケンジは今晩、どうすると言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじはこんばん、どうするといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji wa konban, dou suru to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Game only while the moon is out, which on a full-moon night means until morning.
Stop gaming as soon as the moon comes out.
Go outside to look at the full moon instead of gaming.

questions.explanation: Line 13: tsuki ga deteru aida dake ni suru. Deteru means the moon is out, a state that lasts, not the moment it appears, so 'only while the moon's out'. Kenji first spots it in line 9 (atchi, tsuki ga deteru), just after sunset, and line 10 says it's a full moon (mangetsu). A full moon is up from sunset until morning, which is why his mother says sore, asa made desho! (line 14). B reads deteru as 'comes out'. That would be tsuki ga detara yameru, and the moon was already out. C: nobody suggests going outside.

newWords.english: while, during (tsuki ga deteru aida = while the moon's out)
